title: Richards Quantitative Temporal-Error Readiness and Owner Boundary

trigger.observed_pattern: All currently accepted REFERENCE runtime fixtures are at the baseline cost vector, while scientifically admitted nonzero F-VQ24 Richards trajectories are materially more expensive but rejected and uncommitted.

diagnosis.current_backend_behavior: returns 0 only when full-step and two-half final physical states are bitwise identical, otherwise returns huge(real64)
diagnosis.consequence: Any genuinely evolving Richards state that differs between full and two-half paths is temporally rejected for every finite temporal_tolerance. Retry step reduction cannot provide graded convergence unless exact bitwise identity eventually occurs.

fkt_contract_lock.fkt04_temporal_provenance_scope: committed temporal provenance, contiguous continuation and fail-closed time-origin validation
fkt_contract_lock.interpretation: F-KT deliberately accepts a model-defined scalar quantitative temporal error and does not prescribe Richards-specific scaling.

primary_scientific_probe.purpose: Measure actual full-vs-two-half component differences and their evolution under retry-scale dt without changing production acceptance.

readiness_questions: Which physical components differ between full and two-half F-VQ24 states: pressure head, water content, ponding depth, groundwater level or optional process state?
How do absolute and relative component deltas scale as dt is halved?
Does a monotone convergence signal exist over the current retry ladder?
Can a dimensionally explicit scalar metric be defined without hidden fixed scales or mixing incompatible units?
Are existing numerical configuration fields sufficient, or is an explicit Richards temporal-error contract/configuration required before implementation?
claim_limit: F-MR16 currently records a source-grounded readiness diagnosis only. It does not authorize changing the temporal metric, tolerance, retry policy, mass gate or production acceptance. A production change is forbidden until the F-VQ24 full-vs-two-half state deltas are characterized and the metric semantics are explicit and dimensionally defensible.
next_action: Build a read-only F-VQ24 temporal-delta characterization harness on the exact F-VQ27 source postimage and measure componentwise full-vs-two-half differences over the retry-scale dt ladder.
